name: KPI Green Energy Ltd
title: KPI Green Energy Ltd - 542323 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: KPI Green FY26 PAT Rs509cr (+57%) on IPP ramp, but inventory up ~4x, interest up ~130% and CPP order book (Rs5,246cr) fell short of the Rs6,000cr cited last quarter; execution risk rising.

summary.headline: KPI Green FY26 total income rose 56% to INR2,742 crore and PAT 57% to INR509 crore; management guides 40-50% growth.
summary.overview: FY26 total income reached INR2,742 crore (up 56% YoY), EBITDA INR1,006 crore (up 73%) and PAT INR509 crore (up 57%). Q4 FY26 total income was INR810 crore, EBITDA INR305 crore and PAT INR155 crore. Installed capacity stood at over 1.62 GW with 4.64 GW under work-in-progress, and operating cash flow rose to INR424 crore from INR208 crore. Interest cost rose sharply (about 130% to INR182 crore) as IPP capacity was commissioned ahead of full revenue, and management defended the margin and ROE trajectory with FY27-28 as the inflection years.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA margin about 36.6% excluding other income, per analyst

segments.name: IPP (independent power producer)
segments.commentary: Management cites about 85-90% EBITDA margin for IPP and an expected annual output above 390 crore units. Interest cost was about INR182 crore, against IPP contribution described as about 9%. Installed-plus-WIP IPP capacity is 2.57 GW.

segments.name: CPP / EPC
segments.commentary: CPP order book stated at about INR5,246 crore, with about INR1,500 crore executed on the larger orders. EPC EBITDA margin is about 16-18%. Installed plus upcoming CPP portfolio is 3.69 GW.

segments.name: Subsidiary Sundrops Energia
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR586 crore, PBT INR130 crore and PAT INR97 crore. Management plans a DRHP filing for an IPO this financial year, focused on BESS and battery manufacturing.

guidance_outlook: Revenue and profit growth of 40-50% YoY; management says this is maintained, with a related 40-50% CAGR to FY30 per an analyst question.
Management targets ROE returning to earlier levels next year, after the FY26 dip driven by interest and depreciation.

IPP capacity of about 1.7 GW targeted for commissioning in FY27 (DC basis), with the 250 MW and 370 MW projects due October 2026, the 150 MW wind project November 2027, and a 300 MW SJVN project awaiting PPA signature.
Botswana subsidiary: first commitment of 500 MW by December 2027; PPAs to be signed shortly.
Target of 10 GW by 2030, which management says it expects to reach ahead of schedule.
capex_capacity: As on March 31, 2026: installed capacity over 1.62 GW, WIP over 4.64 GW, total installed plus upcoming about 6.26 GW (2.57 GW IPP, 3.69 GW CPP).
IPP capacity was about 965 MW as of March 31, 2026; management says it has crossed 1 GW since.
Peak IPP interest cost estimated at around INR300 crore; IPP breakeven per project 6-7 years.
Khavda 240 MW project billing started, with a delay of about 6-7 months due to GSECL substation; the remaining portion expected to complete by quarter-end.
Land bank of 7,210 acres, of which about 800-1,000 acres is owned and the rest is held on 26-27 year leases.
demand_pricing: CPP order book about INR5,246 crore; management says this equates to roughly 2.7 GW, though the analyst's order-book reconciliation was not fully resolved.
Inventory about INR1,400 crore, held at 30-40% of the order book, which management says is needed for timely execution amid geopolitical supply risk.
Win ratio historically about 75%; bid pipeline of 4-5 GW, with management saying it will be more selective toward higher-margin tenders.
BESS: two signed orders with GUVNL, 440/890 MWh and 120/240 MWh; management says BESS margins will be lower than IPP and VGF of INR18-27 lakh/MW affects returns.
Input cost: panels and turbines are 60-70% of project cost; advances to manufacturers and inventory build are used to hedge price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Peak interest burden and when IPP becomes EPS accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak interest cost is estimated at about INR300 crore, with phased commissioning reducing the drag. Full-year IPP operation in FY27-28 should bring strong cash flows; management expects ROE to start recovering next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory of about INR1,400 crore is 30-40% of the order book, built to execute orders on time given geopolitical supply risk on turbines and panels.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter pledge timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of promoter shares are pledged against SBI's INR3,000 crore sanction. Release is tied to COD of the 250 and 370 MW projects, with full release expected by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Botswana funding and equity structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Botswana will be a step-down subsidiary under FEMA ODI rules, which allow investment up to 4x the parent net worth. Management says it has in-principle approvals from international funds for the equity portion.

qa_highlights.question: Grid stabilization charges in Maharashtra?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is still evaluating project feasibility. It is not a rooftop player, and grid stabilization charges are not present in Gujarat.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income, depreciation and finance cost up so much?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income rose on fixed-deposit interest. Depreciation and finance cost rose with about double the asset base and higher working capital limits, following the FY25 QIP.

risks_watch: Interest and depreciation rising ahead of IPP revenue; EPS and ROCE dilution could persist into FY27 (ROCE reportedly fell from about 18-19% to 13-14%).
Working capital and inventory build (inventory days rose sharply); the CPP order book reconciliation was unclear on the call.
Maharashtra grid stabilization charges and their effect on CPP project feasibility.
Curtailment of renewables during peak hours and CTU transmission timelines of 2028-2030.
Promoter pledge release tied to COD and SBI sanction; full release targeted by March 2027.
Management's growth guidance has moved from 50-60% to 40-50% per analysts' notes; the company says the sector growth rate has slowed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and execution, but defensive when pressed on the growth guidance change, the margin trajectory and the interest drag. Several answers on the BESS margin, the CPP order book and capacity targets were vague or deferred. Call quality was poor and several analyst questions went unanswered.
key_quotes: So automatically, the interest cost has increased this year.
And evacuation is not the bottleneck for our growth.
In the past, our win ratio has been at 75%. But going forward, we'll be very selective.
So, the more the EPC segment, the margin will come a little bit -- will get a little bit strained.

Khavda 240 MW project billing started; remaining portion expected to complete by quarter-end (delayed 6-7 months by GSECL substation)
300 MW SJVN project awaiting PPA signature
Botswana subsidiary first commitment of 500 MW by December 2027; PPAs to be signed shortly

growth.why: Management guides 40-50% revenue and PAT growth (midpoint 45%) for FY27, backed by ~1.7 GW IPP commissioning targeted in FY27, a CPP order book of about INR5,246 crore and Khavda 240 MW billing starting; timelines and PPA signings remain partly open.
